a: Their circuits have two states, on and off, which represent 1 and 0
Because binary is shorter to write
Because people find binary easy to read
Because it uses less electricity than decimal
tasks.fb: Two reliable states are much easier to build than ten.

tasks.q: Which of these is stored in binary inside a computer?
a: All of them: numbers, text, images and sound

tasks.q: How many bits are in a byte?
tasks.fb: Half a byte, 4 bits, is a nibble.

tasks.q: Show the number 5 in binary. Use the last four bits, as a nibble.
tasks.fb: 5 is 0101 in a nibble, which is 00000101 in a byte.

tasks.q: Put these units in order, smallest first.
tasks.fb: Each unit after byte is 1,000 times the one before.

tasks.q: How many megabytes are in a gigabyte?
How many bytes are in 2 kB?
A file is 6,000 MB. How big is it in gigabytes?
tasks.fb: Divide by 1,000 to go up a unit.

tasks.q: What does a lowercase b mean, as in 34 Kb?
a: Kilobits, used for data transmission speeds
Nothing: it means the same as KB
tasks.fb: Uppercase B is bytes, for storage; lowercase b is bits, for speeds.

tasks.q: Show the number 65 in 8-bit binary. This is the code for the letter A.
tasks.fb: 65 is 01000001, which is the ASCII code for A.

tasks.q: What is the largest number a byte can store?
tasks.fb: 8 bits give 256 different values, from 0 to 255.

tasks.q: How many gigabytes are in a petabyte?
tasks.fb: GB → TB → PB is two steps of 1,000.

tasks.q: Roughly how many 8 GB memory sticks would hold 1 TB?
Sort these into the correct unit.
tasks.fb: Each step up the units multiplies by 1,000.

info.title: 1,000 or 1,024?
info.text: Strictly, 1,024 bytes is a kibibyte (KiB). OCR uses 1,000 for a kilobyte, so use 1,000 in the exam.

info.title: Why 8 bits?
info.text: A byte settled at 8 bits because it holds one character in early character sets, and 8 is a convenient power of two.

info.title: Nibble
info.text: A nibble really is the official name for half a byte: computer scientists do occasionally have a sense of humour.

info.title: Exabytes
info.text: After petabyte comes exabyte, then zettabyte. The world now creates well over 100 zettabytes of data a year.

info.title: Advertised sizes
info.text: A '1 TB' drive shows as about 931 GB in Windows, because Windows divides by 1,024 while the manufacturer used 1,000.

info.title: Bits for speed
info.text: Broadband is sold in megabits per second. 80 Mb/s is only 10 MB/s of actual files, because there are 8 bits in a byte.
